To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) there are many new physics signals that can be discovered at the LHC in the first 10 pb − 1 of data; (ii) many of these signals have small standard model backgrounds and are thus easily visible; (iii) the signals are often very similar to those of well-known models that are usually discussed for multi-f b − 1 data sets; (iv) the signals often involve resonances, which could be discovered with a simple search strategy; and (v)

the LHC is sensitive to a large class of new physics models in the early data, even with only 0.1 fb −1, and the LHC will have a sensitivity to new physics in the first year that is much larger than that of the LHC with 10 fb−1.
